conventions: The chain דִּין כָּל־בְּנֵי X is written twice in this chapter (31.5, 31.8) and is divided the same way in both, the division following the ASV's word count rather than the Hebrew: כֹּל takes the recast construct relation together with its own quantifier — *of all* at 31.8, *due to any* at 31.5 — under rule 19; the final noun takes the supplied relative with its copula and predicate — *as are left desolate*, *that is afflicted* — under rules 46 and 20; and בְּנֵי takes an English word only where one is left over, which is *such* at 31.8 and nothing at 31.5, where it is `unrepresented` under rule 22. BSB represents that 31.5 בְּנֵי; the disagreement is this convention and not an error.

Where one substantive is rendered by a multi-word English phrase, this chapter heads it by rule 31's subtraction and never on the generic English noun: שֵׁכָר → *strong drink* heads on *strong* (31.4, 31.6), סָדִין → *linen garments* on *linen* (31.24), מַרְבַדִּים → *carpets of tapestry* on *carpets* (31.22), שֵׁשׁ → *fine linen* on *linen* (31.22). The ASV writes none of *drink*, *garments*, *tapestry* alone for a word of that class here, so rule 31's tie-break does not reach them; each unit names the competing head under rule 8, and a later verse added to this chapter should follow the same reading.
report: Read all 31 verses end to end against the 36-lemma candidate table and against the nine `added` units, which the table cannot see. No construction is analysed two ways with nothing in the source or in the ASV to license the difference, so patches is empty.

The one candidate that looked like a real split is the chain דִּין כָּל־בְּנֵי X, written twice, at 31.5 and 31.8. Both verses divide it on the same principle: כֹּל takes the recast construct relation together with its own quantifier (*of all*, *due to any*) under rule 19, and the final noun takes the supplied relative with its copula and predicate (*as are left desolate*, *that is afflicted*) under rules 46 and 20. They differ only where the ASV differs. 31.8 writes a third noun-phrase word, *such*, which goes to the present בְּנֵי because a present morpheme takes its English before a supplied reading does (rule 46's first rider); 31.5 writes *any that* and leaves בְּנֵי nothing, so it is `unrepresented` under rule 22. That is the English word count, not a split.

Other candidates checked and dismissed as ASV-licensed: מִפְּרִי יָדֶיהָ rendered *With the fruit* at 31.16 and *of the fruit* at 31.31, one preposition taking whichever word was written for it; לְ with a suffix aligned to *for herself* at 31.22 but `unrepresented` at 31.31, which is rule 40's bare indirect object תְּנָה לִּי → *give me* exactly; שָׁלַח rendered *layeth* at 31.19 and *reacheth forth* at 31.20, the particle staying with the verb only where the ASV writes one; the assimilated [הַ] tokens, each read off whether a *the* is written (aligned at 31.19, 31.20 twice, 31.23, 31.24, 31.31; `unrepresented` at 31.3, 31.4 twice, 31.18); and *Nor* resting on the bare waw at both 31.3 and 31.4, the negative being gapped in each.

The nine `added` units were audited as a set, since the lemma table is blind to them, and each falls into a family the chapter handles one way throughout: the impersonal *it* of a verbless clause (31.4 twice, 31.15), which rule 20 excludes from the construction-supplied frame while the copula goes to the predicate — to the לְ heading the prepositional predicate at 31.4 under rule 49, to the predicate noun לַיְלָה at 31.15 under rule 20; a supplied lexical verb (31.4 *to say*, 31.28 *saying*) under rule 20's supplied-lexical-verb clause; a supplied object pronoun with no object morpheme (31.24 *them*) under rule 44; a supplied possessive with no suffix in the phrase (31.15 *their*) under rule 18's closing sentence; a supplied *also* beside a waw already holding the *and* written for it (31.28) under rule 51, which is the other side of the waw that does take *also* at 31.15; and a supplied *But* in a clause with no conjunction morpheme in it (31.30) under rule 14's closing sentences.

None of the five BSB disagreements is an error. 31.5 בְּנֵי and 31.29 עַל and 31.31 לָ are all recastings that leave a morpheme no English word — the second is the גָּדַל … מִן → *exceeded* case named in rules 30 and 35, where the comparative recasting *excellest them all* states nothing for the preposition — and the two 31.30 הַ tokens stand on nouns the ASV renders bare (*Grace is deceitful*, *beauty is vain*), which rule 29's last sentence marks `unrepresented`. Each is a documented convention difference: BSB attaches such a morpheme to its host phrase.

Head choices under rule 31 were checked across the chapter and agree: שֵׁכָר → *strong drink* heads on *strong* at both 31.4 and 31.6, סָדִין → *linen garments* on *linen*, מַרְבַדִּים → *carpets of tapestry* on *carpets*, שֵׁשׁ → *fine linen* on *linen*. Each of those units names its competing head under rule 8.
